**Bounded answer: No.** With `Client(transport=<custom>, trust_env=True)` and no explicit proxy, no environment-proxy transports are constructed, and no mount entries are created from the environment.

The `HTTPTransport(...)` fallback (731–738) is not executed, so trust_env/verify/etc. are not applied anywhere client-side. (In the no-transport case, trust_env is forwarded to HTTPTransport at 734, where per default.py:153 it only feeds `create_ssl_context` — TLS trust-store env handling, not proxy mounting.)
5. So `get_environment_proxies()` (httpx/_utils.py:30–76) is never called from this path (only reachable via line 246).
6. Lines 711–714: explicit `mounts`, if given, update `self._mounts`; line 716 sorts by URLPattern priority.

Selection: `_transport_for_url` (760–769) iterates sorted `self._mounts` and returns first `pattern.matches(url)`; with no mounts, returns `self._transport` (769) — the custom transport. So every request goes through the custom transport even though HTTP(S)_PROXY etc. are set.

Contrast explicit proxy argument: `proxy` non-None bypasses the env branch entirely: `_get_proxy_map` else-branch (249–251) returns `{"all://": proxy}` regardless of `transport`/`allow_env_proxies` — note allow_env_proxies only gates env proxies, not the explicit proxy. Then mounts build at 697–709 becomes one entry, `{"all://": HTTPTransport(..., proxy=proxy)}` via `_init_proxy_transport` (740–758). Important consequence: even with a supplied custom transport, an explicit `proxy=` creates an `all://` mount that `_transport_for_url` matches for every URL (priority ordering places the bare `all://` catch-all last, but it matches everything, since scheme/host/port are all empty → matches() at 192–203 only checks non-empty parts), so requests would use the newly constructed proxy transport, not the custom transport, which then only serves... actually with all:// matching everything, the custom transport would never be selected. So explicit proxy + custom transport effectively overrides it. Also env proxies are still skipped in this case (allow_env_proxies False with custom transport), so `proxy=` + custom transport mounts only the explicit one.

Explicit mounts: `mounts` dict update at 711–714 overwrites env/explicit-proxy-derived entries with the same URLPattern key (dict update). A value of `None` is meaningful: it stores URLPattern→None (713). In `_transport_for_url`, line 767: `return self._transport if transport is None else transport` — a matched None mount selects the client's default transport, i.e., the custom transport; it acts as an explicit "no proxy / use default" opt-out for that pattern. Sort order (URLPattern.priority, _utils.py:205–217): port first (0 < 1), then longer hosts (-len), then longer schemes; so e.g. `all://example.com` (priority (1, -11, 0)) sorts before bare `all://` (1, 0, 0), and bare `all://` is least specific — first match wins in iteration order (765–766). A `None` mount on a more specific pattern therefore shields those URLs from a broader proxy mount and yields the custom transport.

Also mention: since `transport is None` gate applies equally in AsyncClient (1399–1424), behavior is symmetric; sync is what was asked.
